symptoms: You will see gum oozing out from the bark which then hardens.
The leaves turn yellow and start to fall off.
Twigs begin to dry up as the damage gets worse.
The tree eventually dies because the pest stops the flow of sap.
favourable_conditions: The pest infestation is more severe in neglected plantations and during the summer months.
prevention: Keep your plantation clean and well cared for to avoid attracting the pest.
Monitor trees that are more than two years old as they are most at risk.
practices: Regularly check your trees for signs of gumming or tunnels.
Remove and destroy any parts of the tree that are heavily infested.
Keep the plantation clean to prevent the pest from spreading.
